paper.title_en: Charm and beauty production in pp collisions with ALICE
paper.abstract_en: Measurements of charm and beauty production in proton--proton (pp) collisions provide crucial tests of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) and unique access to heavy-quark hadronisation. In this contribution, a selection of recent ALICE results, with emphasis on LHC Run 3 measurements, is presented. The transverse-momentum-differential production cross sections of prompt D mesons at $\sqrt{s}=5.36$ and 13.6 TeV and of fully reconstructed B mesons at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV are discussed together with comparisons to theoretical calculations. The rapidity dependence of charm and beauty production and the $\rm D^{*+}/D^0$ and $\rm Λ_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios provide complementary constraints on heavy-quark production and hadronisation. Measurements of the fractions of ${\rm J}/ψ$ and $ψ({\rm 2S})$ originating from beauty-hadron decays, and of the inclusive $ψ({\rm 2S})$-to-${\rm J}/ψ$ production ratio, further constrain the interplay between perturbative heavy-quark production and non-perturbative bound-state formation.
